name: software-implementation
title: Software Implementation
description: Implement programs and algorithms from a precise technical brief.
procedure:
1. Translate the brief into explicit inputs, outputs, invariants, and failure cases.
2. Inspect the supplied code and preserve its public interfaces unless the task requires a change.
3. Implement the smallest complete solution, keeping ordering and serialization deterministic.
4. Exercise normal, boundary, and malformed inputs and compare every artifact with the stated contract.
notes: Do not replace a required implementation with a hard-coded answer or task-specific fixture.

name: debugging-repair
title: Debugging and Repair
description: Reproduce failures, isolate root causes, and make minimal validated repairs.
procedure:
1. Reproduce the failure with the smallest command that preserves the symptom.
2. Capture the first causal error, relevant state, and stack or debugger evidence rather than the last cascading message.
3. Trace the violated invariant to its producer and patch that point with the narrowest change.
4. Re-run the reproducer and focused regression checks, including a nearby non-failing case.
notes: Preserve unrelated behavior and do not silence errors that reveal an unsatisfied contract.

name: build-compile-porting
title: Build, Compile, and Port
description: Build source trees, resolve compiler issues, and port software across runtimes or architectures.
procedure:
1. Identify the required compiler, target architecture, build entry point, and expected artifact.
2. Start from a clean build and capture the exact first compiler or linker failure.
3. Correct source, flags, dependencies, or ABI assumptions without weakening diagnostics.
4. Rebuild from clean state and execute the produced artifact on the requested target or compatibility check.
notes: A successful incremental build is insufficient; verify a clean reproducible build.

name: testing-validation
title: Testing and Validation
description: Design and run deterministic checks against stated output contracts.
procedure:
1. Convert each acceptance statement into an observable assertion.
2. Run the narrowest relevant checks first, then the complete available suite.
3. Inspect exit status and produced files; do not treat command completion as success.
4. Repeat nondeterminism-sensitive checks and record the exact validation command and result.
notes: Never modify or bypass the benchmark verifier to make a task pass.

name: optimization-performance
title: Optimization and Performance
description: Improve runtime, memory, scheduling, or objective quality under explicit constraints.
procedure:
1. State the objective, constraints, baseline, and measurement method before changing the solution.
2. Profile or derive the true bottleneck and preserve feasibility as a hard condition.
3. Apply the smallest algorithmic, formulation, or resource-scheduling improvement.
4. Measure against the same baseline and verify objective value, constraints, and output equivalence.
notes: Report improvements only from comparable runs; a faster invalid result is a regression.

name: structured-data-processing
title: Structured Data Processing
description: Parse, reconcile, transform, and emit structured datasets with exact schemas.
procedure:
1. Inspect source encodings, schemas, keys, null conventions, and duplicate policy.
2. Normalize fields without losing identifiers or silently coercing invalid values.
3. Join, aggregate, or transform with explicit cardinality and ordering rules.
4. Write the exact requested schema and re-read the result to verify row counts, keys, types, and determinism.
notes: Validate join cardinality explicitly; accidental many-to-many joins commonly create plausible but wrong outputs.

name: scientific-computation
title: Scientific Computation
description: Implement numerical or statistical methods with stable, reproducible calculations.
procedure:
1. Fix units, shapes, precision, seeds, and the mathematical convention required by the brief.
2. Choose a numerically stable formulation and check domain assumptions before computing.
3. Compare intermediate quantities with a small analytic or independently calculated case.
4. Emit values at the requested precision and rerun to confirm reproducibility and tolerance compliance.
notes: Do not round intermediate values unless the specification explicitly requires it.

name: security-recovery
title: Security and Recovery
description: Analyze security failures and recover protected, damaged, or leaked data safely.
procedure:
1. Preserve the original evidence and work on a copy when recovery is destructive.
2. Identify the format, protection mechanism, trust boundary, and exact success condition.
3. Use the narrowest authorized analysis or recovery method and avoid exposing recovered secrets in logs.
4. Validate integrity or exploit mitigation with an independent check and leave the original evidence unchanged.
notes: Treat credentials and recovered material as sensitive even inside diagnostic output.

name: service-configuration
title: Service Configuration
description: Configure, start, inspect, and validate networked Linux services.
procedure:
1. Inspect the installed service version, active configuration, filesystem layout, and required listener.
2. Make the minimal declarative configuration change with correct ownership and permissions.
3. Run the service's syntax or configuration check before reload or restart.
4. Validate the live endpoint and logs from the client side, including persistence across a clean restart when required.
notes: A running process is not proof of a working service; exercise the requested protocol.

name: git-repository-management
title: Git Repository Management
description: Inspect, repair, rewrite, merge, and serve Git repository history.
procedure:
1. Inspect refs, graph, status, remotes, and reflogs without altering repository state.
2. Identify the exact commits and reachability relationship involved in the task.
3. Apply the smallest deterministic ref, index, merge, or history operation while preserving unrelated history.
4. Verify the resulting graph, worktree, object reachability, and requested content from a fresh Git query.
notes: Create a recoverable reference before rewriting or deleting reachable history.

name: machine-learning-modeling
title: Machine Learning Modeling
description: Train, recover, transform, or run machine-learning models and their weights.
procedure:
1. Establish the model architecture, tensor shapes, preprocessing, dtype, device, and checkpoint format.
2. Load or reconstruct weights with explicit missing and unexpected-key checks.
3. Run inference or training with deterministic seeds and correct evaluation mode and gradients.
4. Validate on a small known input, then serialize outputs or weights in the exact required format.
notes: Matching file format alone is insufficient; verify numerical behavior after loading or conversion.

name: media-processing
title: Media Processing
description: Analyze or transform images, video, rendered scenes, and OCR inputs.
procedure:
1. Probe the input media for dimensions, timing, channels, codec, and color or coordinate conventions.
2. Apply transformations without discarding required metadata or changing frame/sample order.
3. Render or encode with explicit deterministic parameters and requested output geometry.
4. Re-open the artifact and validate format, count, dimensions, duration, and task-specific visible content.
notes: Do not infer success from a non-empty file; decode and inspect the generated artifact.

name: formal-reasoning
title: Formal Reasoning
description: Construct formal proofs, interpreters, or semantics-preserving transformations.
procedure:
1. State the judgment, assumptions, syntax, and semantics that the result must preserve.
2. Decompose the goal into lemmas or evaluator cases with explicit invariants.
3. Construct the proof or transformation using only admitted primitives and total cases.
4. Run the checker or interpreter and test boundary constructs that distinguish the intended semantics.
notes: Do not use admitted axioms, unchecked shortcuts, or host-language behavior unless allowed explicitly.

name: systems-emulation
title: Systems and Emulation
description: Work with architectures, virtual machines, low-level formats, and emulators.
procedure:
1. Identify guest architecture, binary format, firmware or kernel, devices, and expected boot interface.
2. Inspect artifacts with architecture-aware tools before execution.
3. Configure the emulator and cross-toolchain explicitly, including networking, storage, and headless I/O.
4. Validate the requested guest behavior from outside the emulator and preserve boot or console diagnostics.
notes: Host execution success does not validate a cross-architecture artifact; test it in the intended environment.

name: database-recovery-querying
title: Database Recovery and Querying
description: Recover database state and write or optimize exact data queries.
procedure:
1. Preserve database files and inspect schema, journal mode, integrity status, and transaction state read-only.
2. For recovery, replay or extract committed state into a new database; for querying, define exact result semantics first.
3. Apply the minimal recovery or query-plan change with transactions and explicit ordering.
4. Run integrity checks and independently verify row counts, keys, constraints, and requested results.
notes: Never experiment directly on the only copy of a damaged database or its WAL/journal files.

name: concurrency-scheduling
title: Concurrency and Scheduling
description: Reason about asynchronous execution, batching, parallelism, and resource schedules.
procedure:
1. Model tasks, dependencies, resource limits, cancellation, and completion semantics explicitly.
2. Separate correctness-critical ordering from work that may run concurrently.
3. Bound queues and workers, propagate failures and cancellation, and avoid waiting while holding shared resources.
4. Test deterministic edge cases for empty work, partial failure, cancellation, saturation, and clean shutdown.
notes: Throughput improvements must not change result ordering or leave orphan work unless the contract permits it.

name: package-distribution
title: Package Distribution
description: Build and expose installable packages and package repositories reproducibly.
procedure:
1. Inspect package metadata, version, build backend, dependencies, and required index layout.
2. Build artifacts from a clean source tree using the declared environment.
3. Validate wheel or archive contents and metadata before exposing them through the repository.
4. Install from the configured index into a clean environment and import or execute the installed package.
notes: Test through the consumer-facing index URL, not only from a local artifact path.

name: document-processing
title: Document Processing
description: Extract, restructure, typeset, or validate complex documents.
procedure:
1. Identify the document structure, encoding, fonts, assets, and exact requested output format.
2. Preserve semantic hierarchy while extracting or transforming content and references.
3. Build or render with deterministic paths and resolve missing assets and cross-references.
4. Re-open the final document and validate page count, searchable text, links, layout, and required content.
notes: A successful typesetter exit can still produce clipped or missing content; inspect the rendered result.

name: probabilistic-modeling
title: Probabilistic Modeling
description: Fit, sample, and translate Bayesian and probabilistic models.
procedure:
1. Specify variables, support, priors, likelihood, conditioning, and requested estimands.
2. Check data encoding and identifiability before compilation or fitting.
3. Run seeded chains or structure learning with explicit diagnostics and convergence settings.
4. Validate convergence, effective sample size or fit, and posterior summaries before serializing results.
notes: A completed sampler is not evidence of convergence; inspect diagnostics across chains.

name: cryptanalysis
title: Cryptanalysis
description: Implement and validate attacks or recovery procedures for cryptographic constructions.
procedure:
1. Identify the primitive, representation, key schedule, known data, and exact recovery target.
2. Reproduce the relevant round or validation function on a small known vector.
3. Implement the stated analysis with explicit byte order, modular arithmetic, and candidate filtering.
4. Verify recovered material by independently decrypting or matching the original validation relation.
notes: Keep the search deterministic and validate candidates cryptographically rather than by plausibility alone.

name: repository-recovery
title: Repository Recovery
description: Recover or sanitize repository history without losing required content.
procedure:
1. Freeze destructive operations and inventory refs, reflogs, unreachable objects, and sensitive paths.
2. Create recovery refs for every object that may be needed.
3. Recover or rewrite the minimal ancestry while preserving required branches, tags, authorship, and content.
4. Verify reachability and absence requirements across all refs, then confirm the worktree from a fresh clone or checkout.
notes: Deleting a branch does not remove sensitive objects from other refs or reflogs.

name: model-parallelism
title: Model Parallelism
description: Partition neural computation across devices with correct synchronization.
procedure:
1. Record the reference single-device graph, tensor shapes, parameters, and outputs.
2. Define partition boundaries, device placement, communication groups, and microbatch schedule.
3. Implement collectives and synchronization with explicit shape and dtype invariants.
4. Compare distributed outputs and gradients with the reference, then test uneven and boundary partition sizes.
notes: Successful launch does not establish correctness; compare numerical results with a non-partitioned reference.

name: constraint-solving
title: Constraint Solving
description: Encode and solve constrained scheduling or feasibility problems.
procedure:
1. Define decision variables, domains, hard constraints, and objective separately.
2. Encode each natural-language condition once and add small sanity instances with known feasibility.
3. Solve with deterministic parameters and extract a complete assignment rather than solver-internal objects.
4. Re-evaluate every constraint and the objective independently on the emitted solution.
notes: Never treat solver status alone as sufficient; validate the serialized assignment.

name: binary-analysis
title: Binary Analysis
description: Inspect executable formats, memory failures, and low-level program behavior.
procedure:
1. Identify architecture, format, symbols, sections, dynamic dependencies, and available crash artifacts.
2. Reproduce under the debugger or inspect the dump without changing the binary.
3. Correlate addresses with symbols, disassembly, registers, stack, and allocation lifetime to find the first invalid state.
4. Confirm the diagnosis with a minimal reproducer or patched rebuild and retain the exact evidence chain.
notes: Account for ASLR, stripped symbols, and architecture before interpreting raw addresses.

name: bioinformatics-primer-design
title: Bioinformatics Primer Design
description: Align biological sequences and design validated primers for molecular assembly.
procedure:
1. Normalize sequence orientation and alphabet and identify insert, vector, junction, and assembly constraints.
2. Align candidate regions and design primers with explicit length, melting temperature, GC, and overhang rules.
3. Reject self-complementary, off-target, or invalid-junction candidates.
4. Simulate the assembled product and report primer sequences with orientation and validation metrics.
notes: Always distinguish the written primer from its annealing region and reverse-complement orientation.

name: editor-macro-automation
title: Editor Macro Automation
description: Design compact, deterministic editor macros for large-scale text transformation.
procedure:
1. Express one transformation as cursor motion, selection, edit, and advance with a stable starting state.
2. Record the macro on a representative line without depending on incidental screen position.
3. Replay on boundary and exceptional lines and make the operation safely repeatable.
4. Apply across the requested range and diff the full output against the transformation rules.
notes: Prefer text-object and search motions over fixed character counts when input widths vary.
